lead: Flynn's models classify a computer by how many instruction streams and data streams it uses at the same time. An instruction stream is the sequence of operations a control unit issues. A data stream is the set of operands those operations work on. The four classes are SISD, SIMD, MISD and MIMD. The names matter in exams and in design: a GPU is SIMD-like, a multicore CPU is MIMD, and a dataflow machine is a different idea. Each class has a clear rule, a common example, and a limit.
prereq: You need: Chapter 1.1 for the levels of parallelism and why parallel processing helps.

sections.h3: Streams and the four Flynn classes

blocks.text: Flynn's models use two counts: instruction streams and data streams. A stream is active at one time. One CPU core fetching and executing one program has one instruction stream. The operands that one instruction works on form one data stream. The four classes come from the possible counts.

SISD is the scalar CPU: one instruction works on one data item. SIMD is a SIMD computer: one control unit issues one instruction, and many ALUs apply it to many data items. MISD has many instruction streams working on one data stream. It is mostly theoretical; no common general-purpose machine uses it. MIMD is a MIMD multiprocessor: each processor or core has its own instruction stream and its own data stream. Shared-memory and distributed-memory forms are in Chapter 1.3.

A SIMD computer has one control unit, many ALUs, and vector or array registers. The control unit fetches one instruction, such as add, and broadcasts it. Each ALU takes its own element from the data stream. All ALUs run in lockstep: they start and finish the same instruction together.

items: The control unit fetches one instruction, for example add.
It broadcasts that instruction to all ALUs.
Each ALU reads its own data element.
All ALUs execute the instruction in lockstep.
Mask bits switch off lanes that must not write.

blocks.text: Array add shows the idea. To compute C[i] = A[i] + B[i], one instruction adds A[i] and B[i] for every active lane i. If n is larger than the lane count, the hardware repeats in chunks. A mask is one bit per lane. Mask bit 1 lets the lane write; 0 makes it idle. Masks handle tails and branches: the hardware computes both sides of an if, then masks select the correct lanes.

Shared-memory SIMD algorithms mean the same operation on many array elements. A vector sum, an image filter, or a matrix row update is written as lane-wise work. The programmer thinks in arrays, not one scalar at a time. GPUs are the common SIMD-like machine today; Unit 3 covers CUDA lanes and warps. A GPU warp runs a group of lanes in lockstep.

A MIMD multiprocessor has many processors. Each processor fetches its own instructions and uses its own data. The processors are independent: one can run a database query while another runs a web server. They can also run different parts of one parallel program. This is the class of most multicore CPUs and cluster nodes.

Two forms matter. In shared-memory MIMD, all processors see one address space; threads communicate by reading and writing shared variables. In message-passing MIMD, each node has private memory; processes communicate by sending messages. MIMD needs synchronization: locks, barriers, or messages. Without it, two threads can update the same counter and lose an update.

SPMD means single program, multiple data. All processes run the same program text, but each has a different rank and works on different data. MPI programs are SPMD. SPMD is a programming style on MIMD machines, not a Flynn class. Do not call it a fifth class. Data parallelism and model parallelism are in Chapter 1.8.

A dataflow machine does not use a program counter to choose the next instruction. It uses a dataflow graph. A node is an operation, such as add or multiply. An edge carries a value. A node fires when all its input operands are ready; then it computes and sends results along output edges.

items: Place values, called tokens, on input edges.
A node is enabled when every input edge has a token.
The node fires: it reads the tokens, computes, and removes them.
It puts result tokens on its output edges.
Repeat until no node is enabled.

blocks.text: An adder with tokens 3 and 4 fires and sends 7. If one input is missing, it waits. This data-driven order is not a Flynn class: Flynn counts instruction and data streams, while dataflow counts readiness of operands. A dataflow graph can expose parallelism: independent nodes fire at the same time. Some processors use dataflow ideas inside schedulers, but a full dataflow machine is not common.

figure.caption: The tree separates the four Flynn classes and shows dataflow as a different idea. SIMD sends one instruction to many lanes in lockstep; MIMD runs independent threads.

spec.aria: A classification tree with a root for machine models and children SISD, SIMD with GPU lanes, MIMD, and dataflow, which is marked as not Flynn.

examples.question: Name the Flynn class for each case. (a) A GPU runs one add instruction on many lanes. (b) An 8-core CPU runs a different program on each core. (c) A scalar CPU adds two registers. (d) A dataflow adder fires when both inputs arrive. Explain each answer in one line.
steps: Read each case for instruction streams and data streams.
(a) One add instruction, many lane data: one instruction stream, many data streams. Class is SIMD.
(b) Eight cores run different programs: many instruction streams, many data streams. Class is MIMD.
(c) One core runs one add on two registers: one instruction stream, one data stream. Class is SISD.
(d) Firing depends on operand arrival, not on a control unit's instruction count. This is dataflow, which is not a Flynn class.
examples.answer: (a) SIMD, (b) MIMD, (c) SISD, (d) dataflow, which is not a Flynn class.

traps: A multicore CPU is MIMD, not SIMD. Many cores alone do not make SIMD; SIMD needs one instruction over many data items.
MISD is mostly theoretical. Do not invent a common MISD computer for an exam answer.
Dataflow is not a Flynn class. Flynn counts streams; dataflow uses operand readiness.
SPMD is a programming style on MIMD, not a fifth Flynn class.
SIMD lockstep does not mean all lanes do useful work. A mask can switch lanes off.

quiz.q: Define instruction stream and data stream in Flynn's classification.
quiz.a: An instruction stream is the sequence of instructions a control unit issues. A data stream is the set of operands those instructions work on.
MISD needs many independent instruction streams working on the same data stream. Few natural workloads fit, and building it is hard. No common general-purpose machine uses it.

quiz.q: A phone applies the same brightness scaling to 64 pixels with one vector instruction. Which Flynn class is this?
quiz.a: SIMD. One instruction stream works on many data items, the 64 pixel values.

quiz.q: An 8-core CPU runs four different programs on separate data. A student calls it SIMD because all cores add numbers. Correct the student.
quiz.a: It is MIMD. Each core has its own instruction stream and its own data. SIMD needs one instruction stream over many data items in lockstep.

quiz.q: In a dataflow graph, an add node has token 5 on the left input and token 2 on the right input. What happens and what is the output?
quiz.a: Both inputs are ready, so the node fires. It computes 5 + 2 and outputs token 7.

quiz.q: How is SPMD different from SIMD?
quiz.a: SPMD is a programming style: the same program text runs on MIMD processes, each with its own instruction stream and data. SIMD is a hardware class: one instruction stream drives many lanes in lockstep.

quiz.q: In a SIMD add over arrays, why use a mask when n is not a multiple of the lane count?
quiz.a: The mask disables extra lanes in the last chunk. Active lanes write valid results; masked lanes stay idle and do not write out of bounds.

beyond: Not for the exam. Dataflow graphs appear in compilers, stream processors, and machine-learning runtimes that schedule operations when inputs are ready. SIMD masks are the basis of vector libraries and GPU kernels. SPMD is the normal style for MPI clusters. Search next for 'dataflow graph scheduling', 'SIMD mask', and 'SPMD MPI'.
